Environmental Ed Day 16 North South East West

Nov 19, 2010 • Janice Cotcher

I started writing this two weeks ago and was not happy with it. I thought a little more about it and made some changes before posting. Hopefully it makes sense. Michael Gatin the acting Director of First Nations and Métis Education in Saskatchewan came to speak to the class yesterday. He started by drawing the following and the chalkboard ! along with some keywords for each

Interconnectedness- East, where the sun rises, infancy, new beginnings, spring, two-legged

He noted that we are dependent on nature; nature does not depend on us. This reminded me when Sir Ken Robinson in his TEDTalks video said that if all the insects disappeared, all life on Earth would vanish within 50 years. If all the humans disappeared, all life on Earth would thrive within 50 years. Kinda doesn’t make us seem very important, does it?

Stewardship- South, the place of family and relationships, adolescents, summer, swimmers

He asked the questions “Are we borrowing against future generations?” and “How sustainable is our dominance?” How appropriate in a society that spends more than they can afford that society uses more resources than it needs. How greedy am I to have a long shower when people in other parts of the world are dying of thirst? How much waste do we produce because it is easy and convenient? As a teacher, I’m always annoyed when students leave my class without cleaning up after themselves. A task that would be easy for each individual becomes a great burden for one. Isn’t that what we are doing to the environment?

Reciprocity - West, where the sun sets, adults, a place of introspection, winged, fall The question that he asked that probably struck me the most was “What have I given back?” I am constantly striving to use less but what have I given back to the environment? What can I give back to the environment? I’m going to have to think about this.

Balance \& Harmony-North – where the snow comes from, the seat of wisdom, old age, winter, four legged He noted that we need to broaden our definition of contribution to society. Often times monetary contributions are vaulted above all others. I’m not sure how this relates to the concept of balance. Maybe I missed the point but I’m definitely going to need to think about it more.

The class went through a simulation of how resources are distributed by deciding how a cake should be divided. Some interesting points that came out of the exercise:

  • Sometimes there is an illusion of scarcity to create demand.
  • People in power decide who gets a share of the resources
  • If you haven’t contributed anything, why do you deserve a share?
  • When groups of people are treated better than others, it is often not questioned

Michael Gatin’s entire talk reminded of

ALL I REALLY NEED TO KNOW I LEARNED IN KINDERGARTEN

All I really need to know about how to live and what to do and how to be I learned in kindergarten. Wisdom was not at the top of the graduate school mountain, but there in the sand pile at school. These are the things I learned:

  • Share everything.
  • Play fair.
  • Don’t hit people.
  • Put things back where you found them.
  • Clean up your own mess.
  • Don’t take things that aren’t yours.
  • Say you’re sorry when you hurt somebody.
  • Wash your hands before you eat.
  • Flush.
  • Warm cookies and cold milk are good for you.
  • Live a balanced life - learn some and think some and draw and paint and sing and dance and play and work every day some.
  • Take a nap every afternoon.
  • When you go out in the world, watch out for traffic, hold hands and stick together.
  • Be aware of wonder. Remember the little seed in the Styrofoam cup: the roots go down and the plant goes up and nobody really knows how or why, but we are all like that.
  • Goldfish and hamsters and white mice and even the little seed in the Styrofoam cup - they all die. So do we.
  • And then remember the Dick-and-Jane books and the first word you learned - the biggest word of all - LOOK.

Everything you need to know is in there somewhere. The Golden Rule and love and basic sanitation. Ecology and politics and equality and sane living.

Take any one of those items and extrapolate it into sophisticated adult terms and apply it to your family life or your work or government or your world and it holds true and clear and firm. Think what a better world it would be if we all - the whole world - had cookies and milk at about 3 o’clock in the afternoon and then lay down with our blankies for a nap. Or if all governments had as a basic policy to always put things back where they found them and to clean up their own mess.

And it is still true, no matter how old you are, when you go out in the world, it is best to hold hands and stick together. [Source: “ALL I REALLY NEED TO KNOW I LEARNED IN KINDERGARTEN” by Robert Fulghum ]
